# Closure and Escalation Notes

**API Probing - One Client Rejected on Many Distinct Paths** · `T1595.003_api_auth_probing` · [T1595.003](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1595/003/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1595.003_api_auth_probing for <c-ip> at <window start, UTC>
Observed:     <n> distinct cs-uri-stem from c-ip <value> in the 5m window: <values>
Checked:      1. Resolve the client address - internal host, VPN pool, cloud provider or a known scanner -> <result>
              2. List the paths and status codes for the window, and the user agent -> <result>
              3. Check whether any request from the same client then succeeded on a protected path -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | cors_preflight (applied) | approved_scanner (proposed)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Single-page applications whose session expired, calling several protected endpoints at once
- Security scanners and API test suites run against the application on purpose

Never tune:
- Never exclude a client address without a replacement: the excluded host is the one an attacker will use.
- Never raise the threshold without re-reading the guarantee: 2T-1 distinct paths is the smallest burst that always alerts (9 for T=5).

```text

              Any successful responses to the same client after the burst -> <where it is saved>
              WAF or proxy records for the client -> <where it is saved>
```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. A protected path answered 200 to the same client after the rejections
2. The client is not a known scanner and the paths cover administration or user data
3. The same client also triggered the object-ID enumeration correlation

Risk conditions: host is critical +15 · outside business hours +10 · approved change window -30.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Block or rate-limit the client address at the WAF or proxy
2. Disable any endpoint found serving data without authentication until it is fixed
3. Revoke sessions or tokens issued to the client
